investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for a remote agent was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 eligible nodes and node affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4 nodes, leaving 0/6 nodes available. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because agent creation never progressed past the scheduling gate.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler reports "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and "2 No preemption victims found," meaning no existing pods on those nodes are lower-priority and evictable. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector, so they are ineligible regardless of resource availability. Because the pod never schedules, the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval runner cannot collect any of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap and a fail status across all three sibling checks.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod\'s node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: pod was stuck unscheduled for 148s before the check timed out (latencyMs=155130, status=fail).
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming agent creation never reached any observable state.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial progress was recorded.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm') with pod stuck for 143s, confirming the resource exhaustion is not isolated to a single probe invocation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error and pod stuck for 148s, confirming the condition persisted across the full eval window (16:03–16:10 UTC).

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1854-1859: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId — if the pod never schedules, neither orgId nor any downstream evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:254-258: the contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], both of which depend on a successfully scheduled and booted VM.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing pods and no preemption candidates exist, so new remote-agent pods cannot be scheduled.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool shrinkage: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any VM slot exhaustion on those nodes.

Tertiary — peer-pod provider quota or infrastructure limit: the underlying VM provider backing kata.peerpods.io/vm may have hit a quota ceiling, preventing the node from advertising additional VM capacity even if pods were evicted.

Lower probability — transient spike in concurrent remote-agent demand: a burst of legitimate or probe-driven agent creation requests may have temporarily saturated the fixed VM slot pool, with no recovery before the eval window closed.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion would not be the cause and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be investigated.

If a subsequent eval run with identical cluster state succeeded and produced all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure would be transient and not attributable to sustained resource exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes that failed affinity/selector matching were found to have sufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the affinity rules were corrected to include them, and the failure persisted, the root cause would shift to the VM provider quota or a different infrastructure layer.
If the eval runner logs showed the pod was scheduled but the agent process failed to start or report state, the root cause would be in the agent runtime rather than the Kubernetes scheduler.

If no pods were found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm on the eligible nodes, the resource exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a node-level driver or device plugin failure would become the primary hypothesis.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all nodes and alerts when available slots fall below a configurable threshold, providing early warning before exhaustion causes agent creation failures.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum (e.g., >= 3) so that shrinkage of the eligible node pool is caught independently of a scheduling failure.

Add a peer-pod provider quota eval that checks the VM backend quota utilization and warns when usage exceeds a high-watermark percentage, catching infrastructure-layer limits before they surface as scheduler rejections.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulerMessage) so that future failures include the rejection reason in the evidence object rather than only in the check message, enabling automated triage.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the eval's agent pod at the time of the run. The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported it as fully consumed, and the 4 remaining nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~143–148 seconds, the eval timed out before createAgent() could return, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) empty and triggering the contract validation failure. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure, not a confirmed user-facing product outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient VM resource quota and 4 nodes rejecting the pod due to node affinity/selector mismatch. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or invoking the runtime, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm schedulable capacity. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible for kata peer-pod workloads and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the VM resource quota on those nodes is fully consumed. The remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector requirements and cannot be used even via preemption. As a result, every eval attempt that requires spawning a remote-agent pod (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) times out unscheduled after ~143–155 seconds, producing no evidence output and failing all three checks. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting the state of the cluster at the time of the run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for a remote agent was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 eligible nodes and node affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4 nodes, leaving 0/6 nodes available. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because agent creation never progressed past the scheduling gate.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler reports "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and "2 No preemption victims found," meaning no existing pods on those nodes are lower-priority and evictable. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector, so they are ineligible regardless of resource availability. Because the pod never schedules, the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval runner cannot collect any of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap and a fail status across all three sibling checks.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod\'s node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: pod was stuck unscheduled for 148s before the check timed out (latencyMs=155130, status=fail).
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming agent creation never reached any observable state.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial progress was recorded.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm') with pod stuck for 143s, confirming the resource exhaustion is not isolated to a single probe invocation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error and pod stuck for 148s, confirming the condition persisted across the full eval window (16:03–16:10 UTC).

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1854-1859: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId — if the pod never schedules, neither orgId nor any downstream evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:254-258: the contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], both of which depend on a successfully scheduled and booted VM.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing pods and no preemption candidates exist, so new remote-agent pods cannot be scheduled.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool shrinkage: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any VM slot exhaustion on those nodes.

Tertiary — peer-pod provider quota or infrastructure limit: the underlying VM provider backing kata.peerpods.io/vm may have hit a quota ceiling, preventing the node from advertising additional VM capacity even if pods were evicted.

Lower probability — transient spike in concurrent remote-agent demand: a burst of legitimate or probe-driven agent creation requests may have temporarily saturated the fixed VM slot pool, with no recovery before the eval window closed.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion would not be the cause and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be investigated.

If a subsequent eval run with identical cluster state succeeded and produced all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure would be transient and not attributable to sustained resource exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes that failed affinity/selector matching were found to have sufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the affinity rules were corrected to include them, and the failure persisted, the root cause would shift to the VM provider quota or a different infrastructure layer.
If the eval runner logs showed the pod was scheduled but the agent process failed to start or report state, the root cause would be in the agent runtime rather than the Kubernetes scheduler.

If no pods were found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm on the eligible nodes, the resource exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a node-level driver or device plugin failure would become the primary hypothesis.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all nodes and alerts when available slots fall below a configurable threshold, providing early warning before exhaustion causes agent creation failures.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum (e.g., >= 3) so that shrinkage of the eligible node pool is caught independently of a scheduling failure.

Add a peer-pod provider quota eval that checks the VM backend quota utilization and warns when usage exceeds a high-watermark percentage, catching infrastructure-layer limits before they surface as scheduler rejections.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulerMessage) so that future failures include the rejection reason in the evidence object rather than only in the check message, enabling automated triage.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing workloads or leaked/stuck pods, leaving zero capacity for new eval pods.
[Likely] A prior eval run or production workload created remote-agent pods that were not cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner may not have completed successfully), holding the VM quota slots.

[Possible] The 4 non-affinity nodes were recently added or reconfigured and have not been labeled/tainted to accept kata peer-pod workloads, reducing the effective scheduling pool from a previously larger set.
[Possible] A cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange for the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was recently tightened, reducing the number of concurrent VMs allowed on the 2 eligible nodes.

[Lower confidence] Node affinity rules on the eval pod spec require a label or taint that is no longer present on 4 of the 6 nodes due to a node configuration change, shrinking the eligible pool to only the 2 already-saturated nodes.

recommendedNextActions: Check the production-api Kubernetes cluster immediately for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on the 2 eligible nodes to determine if quota is fully consumed.

List all pods in the production namespace that request the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and are in Running, Pending, or Terminating state — identify any that are leaked eval pods from prior runs where withCleanup may not have completed.
If leaked pods are found, manually terminate them to free quota and then re-run the eval suite to confirm recovery.

Verify node labels and taints on all 6 cluster nodes to confirm that the 4 nodes rejecting the pod due to affinity/selector mismatch are expected to be ineligible, and that no recent node reconfiguration reduced the eligible pool.

Consider adding a pre-flight check to the remote-agent eval runner that queries cluster capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm before attempting pod creation, and returns a more actionable SKIP or WARN status instead of waiting for the full scheduler timeout (~148s).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes nodes show available kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity greater than zero at the time of the failure, the quota-exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling misconfiguration should be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent workloads temporarily exhausted quota) rather than a sustained capacity problem.

If the 4 non-affinity nodes are found to have the correct labels/taints and the pod spec's nodeAffinity is confirmed unchanged, the node-affinity mismatch would point to a pod spec regression rather than a node configuration change.
If no stuck or leaked kata peer-pod VMs are found consuming quota slots, the exhaustion is due to legitimate concurrent workloads or a hard quota ceiling, not a cleanup failure.

If the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks pass in the same run, that would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote (kata peer-pod) scheduling path and not a broader API or authentication issue.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all eligible nodes and warns when available slots fall below a minimum threshold (e.g., fewer than 2 free slots).

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists all kata peer-pod VMs in the production namespace older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust quota.
Add a node-affinity health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes carry the labels/taints required by remote-agent pods, alerting if the eligible pool shrinks below the expected count.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to emit a structured scheduling-failure evidence key when the pod enters Unschedulable state, so future failures distinguish quota exhaustion from affinity mismatch without requiring manual cluster inspection.
